**Finding: MFN — compliant (preferred position met).**

The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation mechanic at all, in either direction. Section 4 (Fees) and Exhibit B (Pricing, Revenue Sharing Fees, Payment Terms) fix the licence, maintenance, MarketSite.net access, implementation and revenue-share economics without any parity, best-terms, right-to-match or third-party-offer disclosure obligation on Corio. Exhibit D's sales and marketing cooperation provisions are expressly non-binding and address cross-selling incentives, not pricing parity. Nothing therefore obliges us to extend Commerce One terms no less favourable than those given to others, so the preferred position ("no MFN obligation on Customer") is satisfied and no redline is proposed.

Noted for commercial awareness only, not as a deviation: there is likewise no MFN running in our favour, so if best-pricing protection is a negotiating objective it would need to be introduced affirmatively rather than fixed as a playbook defect.
